title: EWS Certificate 2026: Eligibility, ₹8 Lakh Limit & Apply
meta_description: EWS certificate 2026 - eligibility, documents, online application via e-District portal. 10% government job and education reservation for ₹8 lakh income limit.

hero.one_liner: EWS certificate gives 10% reservation in government jobs and education for General category families with annual income below ₹8 lakh

sections.heading: What is an EWS certificate
content: EWS stands for Economically Weaker Section. The certificate is your proof of eligibility for the 10% reservation introduced by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment in 2019.
This reservation is only for General category (unreserved) families with annual household income below ₹8 lakh. It is in addition to SC/ST/OBC reservation, not instead of it.
If you belong to SC, ST, or OBC, you already have a separate reservation and EWS does not apply to you. Only General category candidates can claim EWS.

Before 2019, a General candidate from a family earning ₹3 lakh competed in the same pool as one from a family earning ₹50 lakh. EWS corrects this by giving economically weaker General families their own reserved seats.
Without an EWS certificate you compete in the open General category even if your family income is below ₹8 lakh. If you qualify, it can be the difference between selection and missing the cutoff.

sections.heading: ✅ EWS eligibility criteria
qualify: You are General category, not on any SC, ST, or OBC list
Gross annual family income is below ₹8 lakh for the preceding financial year
Family owns less than 5 acres of agricultural land in total
Residential flat, if any, is under 1,000 sq.ft.
Residential plot is under 100 sq.yards in a notified city, or under 200 sq.yards elsewhere
disqualify: Your caste appears on any SC, ST, or OBC list, so you use that reservation instead
Total family income reaches ₹8 lakh or more from all sources combined
Family holds 5 acres or more of farmland, clubbed across all members
Family owns a flat of 1,000 sq.ft. or larger, regardless of income
A single asset breach disqualifies you even when income is under the limit

sections.heading: How property limits are counted
content: Agricultural land is counted across all family members combined, not per person. If your father owns 3 acres and your mother owns 3 acres, the total is 6 acres and you do not qualify.
The residential flat limit is 1,000 square feet. Owning a flat of that size or larger disqualifies you regardless of income.
Residential plot limits depend on location: 100 sq.yards in a notified municipality, 200 sq.yards in a non-notified area. These rules catch families owning large plots in prime urban locations.
All four property conditions are checked together, not just one. You can be under the income limit and still be disqualified by a single asset breach, so review every line before you apply.

sections.heading: 👨‍👩‍👦 Who counts as family, and whose income is added
content: The word family has a strict legal meaning here, and getting it wrong is the top reason certificates fail verification.
Family means you, your parents, your siblings below 18, your spouse, and your children below 18. That is the full list.
Grandparents, uncles, aunts, and married adult siblings are not counted. Property or income in a grandfather's name is generally left out of the test.
You add the income of everyone inside that family circle, from every source, for the financial year before you apply.
That includes salary, business profit, agriculture, rent, pension, and interest or dividends. The total must stay below ₹8 lakh.

sections.title: 📜 What the official DoPT order says
sections.content:
Per DoPT OM No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res), an EWS is a person not covered by SC, ST, or OBC reservation whose family gross annual income is below ₹8 lakh, counting all sources for the year before applying.

A family is excluded regardless of income if it owns 5 acres or more of farmland, a flat of 1,000 square feet or larger, or an over-limit residential plot. Property in different cities is clubbed together for this test.

sections.heading: How to Apply Online - Step by Step

steps.title: Visit your state's e-District portal
steps.description: Every state has its own portal: UP (edistrict.up.gov.in), Maharashtra (aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in), MP (mpedistrict.gov.in), Rajasthan (sso.rajasthan.gov.in), Delhi (edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in), Haryana (haryanaeservices.gov.in), etc. Search '[Your State] e-District' or visit the state's main website.

steps.title: Register and login with your email/mobile
steps.description: Create an account on the portal using email and mobile number. Verify email and OTP on mobile. Some states use SSO (Single Sign-On) - you can login with SSOID or Aadhaar instead.

steps.title: Search for 'EWS Certificate' service
steps.description: On the dashboard, search for 'EWS Certificate' or 'Economically Weaker Section Certificate'. Click to start the application. Select the type: 'New EWS Certificate Application'.

steps.title: Fill application form with personal & income details
steps.description: Enter: Full name (as on Aadhaar), date of birth, Aadhaar number, address, occupation, father's name/mother's name (as applicable), annual family income (in rupees), source of income (salary/business/agriculture), ITR or income certificate number (if available).

steps.title: Declare property details and caste
steps.description: Declare: (1) Agricultural land ownership (in acres), (2) Residential flat/apartment (yes/no, if yes, then area in sq.ft.), (3) Residential plot (yes/no, if yes, then area in sq.yards and location - city or non-city), (4) Confirm you are GENERAL CATEGORY (not SC/ST/OBC).

steps.title: Upload documents
steps.description: Upload scanned copies (PDF/JPEG, each <1MB): (1) Aadhaar card, (2) Income proof (ITR/Income Certificate/Salary slip), (3) Self-declaration affidavit on stamp paper (₹10-20) with income and property declaration, (4) Ration card (if applicable - some states require), (5) Caste certificate (to prove you're General category - NOT applicable, self-declaration suffices), (6) Address proof (utility bill/bank statement, if different from Aadhaar).

steps.title: Pay fee and submit
steps.description: Fee: ₹10-50 (varies by state, usually ₹25). Pay online via net banking, debit card, or UPI. You'll get an Application Reference Number - save it to track status.

steps.title: SDM/Tehsildar verification
steps.description: The Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) or Tehsildar office verifies your income and property details through revenue records. They may ask for additional documents or conduct an e-verification through online revenue databases. This takes 7-15 days.

steps.title: Certificate issued online
steps.description: Once verified, the EWS certificate is generated and available for download on the portal (PDF). Physical copy can be collected from the SDM office or mailed (5-10 days). Certificate is valid for 1 YEAR from date of issue - remember to renew next year.

sections.heading: Online vs offline, and who issues it
content: Online is available in most states through the e-District portal. Offline means visiting your district SDM or Tehsildar office and filling the prescribed form.
Online applications typically take 7 to 15 working days. Offline applications take 15 to 30 working days, and some states offer expedited processing for an extra fee.
The certificate must be issued by the District Magistrate, Additional DM, Collector, SDM, or Tehsildar of your area. Certificates from village officers, patwari, lekhpal, or agents are NOT valid.
If you have an exam deadline, apply at least one month before the form closing date. Always confirm the issuing officer's designation matches your state's approved authority list.

sections.heading: Who can legally issue an EWS certificate

rows.label: Revenue officers
rows.value: District Magistrate, Additional DM, Collector, Deputy Commissioner, or Additional Deputy Commissioner

rows.label: Magistrates
rows.value: 1st Class Stipendiary, Sub-Divisional, Taluka, or Executive Magistrate

rows.label: Tehsildar level
rows.value: Any Revenue Officer not below the rank of Tehsildar

rows.label: Sub-Divisional Officer
rows.value: SDO of the area where you and your family normally reside

sections.heading: Documents Checklist
rows: Must have - self-declaration alone isn't accepted
ITR (best), Income Certificate from SDM (for non-salaried), Salary slip for last 3 months
On stamp paper (₹10-20) declaring income, property, caste. Sworn before notary or SDM office.
Required in UP, some optional in other states. Check your state portal.
Utility bill, bank statement, or rent agreement if address differs from Aadhaar.
Self-declaration that you're not SC/ST/OBC suffices. Certificate not required.
Required ONLY if you own property - land deed, flat's property papers, etc. to prove measurements.

sections.heading: 📄 Which documents actually get checked
content: Most rejections trace back to one weak document, so it helps to know what each one proves.
Aadhaar and PAN confirm identity and link your income record. Keep the name spelling identical across both.
The income proof is the heart of the file. This is usually a self-declaration or affidavit, backed by a salary certificate or the previous year's ITR where you have one.
Land and property papers matter even if you own little. The verifier reads them to confirm you are under the asset limits, so missing papers stall the file.
A domicile or residence proof ties you to the district where you apply. Without it the local office cannot verify your case.

sections.heading: Document notes that trip people up
content: For income proof, any one works: ITR of the previous financial year, an employer salary certificate, an income certificate from the Tehsildar, or a stamp-paper affidavit for non-salaried applicants.
If you own no property, a rent agreement plus a self-declaration of no property ownership is enough. If you do own property, keep land records and the property tax receipt showing area ready.
The address on your EWS certificate must match your Aadhaar. If there is a mismatch, update Aadhaar first to avoid rejection.

sections.heading: Validity and yearly renewal
content: An EWS certificate is valid for one financial year, April 1 to March 31. A certificate issued on November 15, 2025 is valid only until March 31, 2026.
There is no automatic renewal. You apply fresh every year so your income is reassessed, which is why families crossing ₹8 lakh lose eligibility.
Most exams require the certificate to be valid on the last date of the application form. Check the notification for which financial year's certificate is accepted.
Using an expired certificate, even by one day, is grounds for rejection. Set an April reminder so you always have a current one ready.

sections.heading: ⏳ How long it takes and what happens after you apply
content: After you submit the form, a local revenue official verifies your income and assets. This is usually the Patwari, Lekhpal, or Village Revenue Officer.
They check your declaration against land records and any income proof you attached. Field verification is why the process is not instant.
Most states issue the certificate within 7 to 21 days once verification clears. Timelines vary by state and by how busy the local office is.
The certificate is then signed by the Tehsildar, SDM, or District Magistrate. Only these authorities can issue a valid EWS certificate.
If details do not match records, the application is sent back or rejected. You can reapply after fixing the specific point that failed.
Keep the acknowledgement or application number the portal gives you. It is the only way to track status or raise a grievance later.
A fresh certificate for each financial year is safest for exams. Apply in March or April so it is ready before recruitment notifications open.

sections.title: 🗓️ Apply every April, don't wait for a notification
sections.content:
An EWS certificate takes 7 to 30 days to process. If you wait for an exam notification to drop, you may miss the deadline.

Apply for a fresh certificate every April, even with no exam in mind. A ready, valid certificate means you can apply for any exam instantly.

sections.heading: What the EWS application form asks for
content: The DoPT-prescribed form (Annexure-III) collects your personal details, a Yes/No on whether your caste is in any SC/ST/OBC list, and full family details. You also list every place you have lived since birth.

It has an income table (salary, business, agriculture, profession, other) and an asset table for agricultural land, residential flat, and urban or rural plots with area and location. One square yard is treated as 9 square feet.

You sign an undertaking that the information is true, citing liability under Sections 199 and 200 of the Indian Penal Code for a false declaration. The certificate is issued on the Annexure-II format and notes the year it is valid for.

sections.heading: Where EWS reservation applies
content: Central government jobs: UPSC CSE, SSC CGL, SSC CHSL, SSC MTS, IBPS and SBI PO/Clerk, RBI Grade B, Railways, and defence exams like NDA, CDS, and AFCAT. EWS gets 10% of vacancies, separate from SC/ST/OBC.
State government jobs: most states follow the central framework for State PSC, police, and teacher recruitment. A few states still have legal challenges pending, so check your state.
Higher education: IITs via JEE Advanced, NITs via JEE Main, medical colleges via NEET, plus central universities and IIMs all keep roughly 10% EWS seats. The EWS cutoff is usually lower than General.
Where it does NOT apply: private sector jobs, private unaided colleges, and promotions within government service. EWS reservation covers initial recruitment only, not promotions.

sections.heading: 🎯 What the 10% reservation actually gets you
content: The EWS quota is a straight 10% of seats or posts, over and above the existing SC, ST, and OBC reservation.
In education it means reserved seats in central institutions like IITs, IIMs, NITs, and central universities.
In jobs it means a 10% share in central government recruitment, from UPSC and SSC to banking and railways.
Many recruitments also give EWS candidates the same relaxed cut-off marks that other reserved categories receive.
It does not, by itself, grant the age or fee relaxation that SC and ST candidates get, unless the specific notification says so.

sections.title: ⚠️ EWS gives a quota, not age or fee relaxation
sections.content:
In exams like AFCAT, UPSC, and SSC, EWS gives you a 10% reservation but no age relaxation and no fee concession beyond what General candidates get.

So in AFCAT, EWS candidates pay the same examination fee and follow the same age limits as General. The only benefit is the reserved 10% of seats with a typically lower cutoff.

sections.heading: ⚖️ EWS vs OBC: the key difference

items.title: EWS is purely economic
items.sub: Based on income and assets within the General category. No caste list is involved at any step.

items.title: OBC is caste-based
items.sub: Your caste must be on a central or state OBC list, and you must be in the non-creamy layer.

items.title: Same income, different route
items.sub: A General family earning ₹5 lakh uses EWS. A listed OBC family uses OBC, even at the same income.

items.title: Category decides, not income alone
items.sub: If your caste is in an SC/ST/OBC list you use that. If you are General, you use EWS.

items.title: Applying as EWS while SC/ST/OBC
items.sub: If your caste is listed you are not eligible, and claiming General status falsely is a criminal offence.

items.title: Leaving out a family member's income
items.sub: The limit is on total family income. ₹3 lakh of yours plus ₹6 lakh of your father's is ₹9 lakh, over the limit.

items.title: Wrong issuing authority
items.sub: Only SDM, Tehsildar, DM, or equivalent can issue it. Village-officer or agent certificates fail verification.

items.title: Using last year's certificate
items.sub: It is valid one financial year only. Apply fresh for the year the notification requires.

sections.title: 🚫 EWS fraud means disqualification and prosecution
sections.content:
Submitting a false certificate by hiding income, misrepresenting property, or claiming General status when you are OBC is a serious offence.

If caught during verification, even years after selection, your appointment is cancelled and you can face a future-exam ban and criminal proceedings. ITR data, property registrations, and Aadhaar records are increasingly cross-checked.

sections.text: 10% EWS reservation opens tens of thousands of extra government job seats and over a lakh educational seats each year for General families below ₹8 lakh. If you qualify, it can lower your cutoff by 5 to 15 marks across UPSC, SSC, banking, and defence exams.

sections.heading: Which portal to use in your state
content: Most states issue the EWS certificate through their own e-District portal, listed below. Search for 'EWS Certificate' or 'Income and Asset Certificate for EWS' once you log in.
If your state has no online service, apply offline at the Tehsildar or SDM office with the documents above. Offline processing usually takes 15 to 30 working days.
Processing times are typical estimates and can vary with verification load. Apply well before any exam or admission deadline to stay safe.

sections.title: 🔗 Official sources and references
sections.content:
Source: Department of Personnel and Training, OM No. 36039/1/2019-Estt.

All figures here are verified against official government notifications. For the latest position, always check your state portal and the recruiting body's notification.

faqs.question: I'm OBC. Can I apply for EWS instead?
faqs.answer:
No. EWS is only for the General (unreserved) category, and if your caste is on any OBC list you must use OBC reservation.

The 'OBC creamy layer can take EWS' idea is legally unsettled and rejected by most state e-District portals. In practice, listed OBC applicants are turned down for EWS.

faqs.question: My father earns ₹6L and I earn ₹4L. Am I eligible?
faqs.answer:
No. Family income is added together, so ₹6L plus ₹4L is ₹10L, which is over the ₹8 lakh limit.

If you are unmarried and living with parents, the total is your income plus both parents' income. Only if the combined figure stays below ₹8 lakh do you qualify.

faqs.question: EWS validity is 1 year. What happens after?
faqs.answer:
You must apply for a fresh certificate every year because family income can change year to year.

For recruitment, the certificate must be valid for the financial year the notification asks for. An expired certificate is rejected.

faqs.question: I own 4.9 acres of agricultural land. Am I eligible?
faqs.answer:
Yes, if you meet all other criteria. The disqualification starts at 5 acres or more, so 4.9 acres is fine.

Your total family income must still be below ₹8 lakh, and the land is counted across all family members combined.

faqs.question: Can I hold EWS certificates from two states at once?
faqs.answer:
No. One person can hold only one EWS certificate at a time.

If you move states you can apply fresh in the new state, but you cannot use certificates from two states simultaneously.

faqs.question: How do I renew my EWS certificate after 1 year?
faqs.answer:
Apply again on your state's e-District portal; the process is the same as the first time.

Renewals often process faster because your earlier details may be pre-filled. There is no automatic renewal.

faqs.question: My EWS certificate was rejected. Why?
faqs.answer:
Common reasons are income over ₹8 lakh, property above the limits, or missing and poor-quality documents.

It can also be rejected if there is a category mismatch or if it was issued by an unauthorised officer. Fix the specific issue and reapply.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for an EWS certificate?
faqs.answer:
Gross annual family income must be below ₹8 lakh for the preceding financial year.

Family means self, parents, spouse, and children below 18, and income from all sources counts: salary, business, agriculture, rent, and interest.

faqs.question: How long is an EWS certificate valid?
faqs.answer:
One financial year, from April 1 to March 31 of the year it is issued for.

A certificate issued in August 2025 for FY 2025-26 is valid until March 31, 2026. After that you need a fresh one.

faqs.question: Can OBC candidates get an EWS certificate?
faqs.answer:
No. EWS is exclusively for the General (unreserved) category.

If your caste is on the central or state OBC list you must use OBC reservation, and you cannot hold both OBC and EWS together.

faqs.question: Where do I apply for an EWS certificate?
faqs.answer:
At your district SDM or Tehsildar office, or online through your state e-District portal.

Examples are edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in for Delhi and edistrict.up.gov.in for UP. The certificate must be issued by SDM, Tehsildar, DM, or equivalent.

faqs.question: What is the full form of EWS?
faqs.answer:
EWS stands for Economically Weaker Section.

The EWS certificate is also called the Income and Asset Certificate, and it proves your eligibility for the 10% General-category reservation.

faqs.question: Does AFCAT have EWS reservation?
faqs.answer:
AFCAT selects into the Air Force, and EWS candidates get the 10% quota but no age or fee relaxation beyond General.

Always read the specific AFCAT notification, as some branches or short-service entries state the exact reservation applied.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for an EWS certificate?
faqs.answer:
You need proof of identity, address, and income or assets.

The core set is Aadhaar, PAN, a passport-size photo, and an income declaration or affidavit. Add land or property records showing owner names, and a domicile or residence proof.

Some states also ask for the previous year's ITR or a salary certificate. Check your state e-District portal for the exact list before you apply.

faqs.question: Is a central EWS certificate different from a state one?
faqs.answer:
The income and asset limits are the same nationwide, set by the central DoPT order.

What differs is the format and issuing portal. A central government job like UPSC or SSC may require the certificate in the central prescribed format.

For a state job or state college, the state format is accepted. Always match the format to the recruiting agency named in the notification.

faqs.question: Does the EWS application process differ by state?
faqs.answer:
The eligibility rules are uniform, but the application portal changes from state to state.

Bihar, Haryana, Gujarat, and West Bengal each use their own e-District or revenue portal. The form fields and upload steps look slightly different on each.

The documents and the ₹8 lakh income test stay the same everywhere. Use the state-wise portal table above to find your correct link.

disclaimer: EWS eligibility criteria and ₹8 lakh income limit are as per the central government notification. Individual states follow the same criteria. Always verify with your state's e-District portal and SDM office for any state-specific variations or recent updates.
